fullPassage:
[1번] One of the most difficult conditions that patients deal with after a stroke is called "hemispatial neglect." This occurs when there is damage to the brain's parietal lobe, which helps process sensory information. When it is damaged, patients cannot perceive people, sounds, and objects on one side of their body. Each of the brain's hemispheres controls the other side of the body, so patients cannot sense what is on the opposite side of the brain damage. For example, a man with damage to the left side of the brain cannot perceive what is on the right. As a result, he might only shave the left side of his face. Similarly, what if a woman suffering from damage to the right side of the brain put on makeup? She would only apply it to the right side of her face.

[2번] Many people are embarrassed by the sound of their own voice. It doesn't bother them when they are having a conversation. But they feel uncomfortable when hearing a recording of it. There is actually a scientific explanation for this. We usually hear our own voice while talking to other people, and when we do so, we receive the sound in two different ways. It arrives externally through the air, just like the sound of other people's voices. But it also arrives internally, because it moves through the bones of our skull. On the other hand, when we hear a recording of our voice, the sound only travels through the air. Sound that travels through bone is perceived as being deeper than sound that travels through the air. So we often find that our voice has a higher pitch than what we expected when we hear it on a recording. Our voice is an important part of our identity. Therefore, it is a little upsetting to find out it doesn't sound like what we thought!

[3번] Light is a mixture of all the colors of the rainbow. Different wavelengths of light are different colors. Blue wavelengths — which help us during the day by improving our mood and increasing our attention span — seem to be the most disruptive at night. Device screens, along with energy-efficient lighting, are increasing the amount of blue wavelengths we are regularly exposed to after sunset. Studies suggest that blue light affects our production of melatonin, a hormone that helps us sleep, more than other types of light. It suppresses melatonin production and damages our sleep patterns. In an experiment, Canadian researchers compared the melatonin levels of two groups of people. One group wore special goggles that blocked blue light while exposed to bright light. The other did not wear goggles and was exposed to regular light. The fact that the melatonin levels of the group without goggles were the same as those of the first group supports the theory that blue light is harming our sleep.

[4번] Brazil's Jungle Marathon, held in the Amazon rainforest every October, is one of the world's most challenging competitions. There are three races — a 42-kilometer marathon, a 127-kilometer four-stage race, and a 254-kilometer six-stage race — that participants can choose from. The six-stage race is clearly the most difficult, taking participants more than a week to complete. The races all go through swamps, across rivers, and along beaches. Only basic necessities such as shelter, first aid, and drinking water are provided, so the runners have to carry their own food and survival equipment. Despite its difficulties and dangers, the event attracts athletes from around the world who can't resist the opportunity to compete in a beautiful natural environment.

[5번] Surprisingly, the English word "alcohol" originally referred to a kind of eyeshadow. In Ancient Egypt, the mineral stibnite was heated to put it through sublimation, the process of turning a solid into a gas. The smoky vapor that was produced left a layer of black powder that could be collected. They used the powder to produce a thick paste, which was then used as eyeshadow. This paste was called kohl, an Arabic term meaning "stain" or "paint." This term was combined with al-, the Arabic word for "the", to create al-kohl, the Arabic word for eyeshadow made from sublimated stibnite. In the mid-1500s, chemists and alchemists discovered this term in ancient textbooks and had a realization that sublimation could draw the purest essence out of something. They began applying this process to liquids produced through a similar process of distillation. Over time, it led to liquors being simply known as "alcohol."

[6번] The "veil of ignorance" is a concept that was first proposed by the political philosopher John Rawls. The idea can be summed up as follows: When setting up laws for a society, you should assume that you could end up in any social position. By doing so, you can avoid being biased by your current situation. Following this way of thinking, people would likely reject slavery because there is a chance that they could find themselves as slaves instead of slave owners. Rawls believed that by keeping the "veil of ignorance" in mind, society would naturally adopt fair, social-democratic policies. When you don't know where you will be on the socioeconomic ladder, strong redistribution and generous social welfare policies become much more attractive.

[7번] Snakes are feared by humans and most animals. There is, however, one animal that does not fear them at all — the mongoose. Not only is it unafraid of snakes, but it also hunts them as prey. The thick fur of the mongoose helps protect it from snake bites, and so does its quickness. It is capable of moving at speeds of more than 30 kph. This, along with its slender body, gives it a great advantage when fighting snakes. Not only can it avoid the jaws of most snake species, but it can also survive when it does get bitten. Rare indeed is the snake venom powerful enough to kill an adult mongoose. The mongoose also has 28 sharp teeth, and it can bite with enough force to crack bones. It fights snakes by focusing on the head, often defeating them by smashing their skull.

[8번] In the Parana Delta near Buenos Aires, Argentina, is a small island called "The Eye," which floats in the middle of a small lake that is about 120 meters in diameter. It was accidentally discovered by Argentinian film director Sergio Neuspiller during the pre-production for a horror film about extraterrestrials. Interestingly, both the island and the lake are perfectly circular. What's more, the lake that surrounds the island is extremely cold and clear — an unusual phenomenon for the area. So mysterious is the island that people have wondered if it was created naturally or by aliens. Since its discovery, researchers have found out that the circular shape might be due to slow-moving water currents flowing to one side of the island. But there is still no explanation for the lake's unusually cold, clear water.

When it is damaged, patients cannot perceive people, sounds, and objects on one side of their body. Each of the brain's hemispheres controls the other side of the body, so patients cannot ②<u>sense</u> ③<u>which</u> is on the opposite side of the brain damage. For example, a man with damage to the left side of the brain cannot perceive what is on the right. As a result, he might only shave the left side of his face. Similarly, what if a woman suffering from damage to the right side of the brain put on makeup? She would only ④<u>apply</u> it to the right side of her face.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: which → what (앞에 선행사가 없으므로 '~하는 것'을 뜻하는 관계대명사 what)
det.analysis:
① called: 'is called ~'는 수동태라 called가 맞아요. 적절합니다.
② sense: 'patients cannot ___'는 조동사 cannot 뒤라 동사원형 sense가 맞아요. 적절합니다.
③ which: 'cannot sense ___ is on the opposite side'에서 밑줄 앞에 꾸며 줄 명사(선행사)가 없어요. 선행사 없이 '~하는 것'을 뜻하려면 관계대명사 what을 써야 해요. which는 앞에 선행사가 있어야 하므로 틀려요. ←정답
④ apply: 'She would only ___'는 조동사 would 뒤라 동사원형 apply가 맞아요. 적절합니다.
det.tip: 선행사가 없을 때 '~하는 것' = 관계대명사 what. which(X, 선행사 필요)

det.korean: what → that (so + 형용사 + that절: 너무 ~해서 …하다)
det.analysis:

② are: 주어 'basic supplies(기본 물품)'는 복수라 복수동사 are provided — 적절

③ what: '너무 힘들어서 완주에 일주일 넘게 걸린다'는 'so + 형용사 + that절' 구문이에요. 그래서 접속사 that이 맞아요. what은 틀림 ←정답

④ attracts: 주어 'the event(그 행사)'는 단수라 단수동사 attracts — 적절
det.tip: so + 형용사 + that + 절 = 너무 ~해서 …하다 (what 아님)

④ 영화 산업 성장에 기여? 본문에 근거 없음 — 오답

③ perceived: 뼈 전달음은 더 깊게 인식됨 — 적절
④ mystery: 목소리가 우리 '수수께끼'의 일부? 목소리는 우리를 규정하는 정체성(identity)의 일부가 원문 ←정답
det.tip: 목소리는 나를 규정하는 identity(정체성)의 일부. mystery(수수께끼)는 부적절

questions.passage: Light is a mixture of all the colors of the rainbow. Different wavelengths of light are different colors. Blue wavelengths — which help us during the day by improving our mood and increasing our attention span — seem to be the most disruptive at night. Device screens, along with energy-efficient lighting, are increasing the amount of blue wavelengths we are regularly exposed to after sunset. Studies suggest that blue light affects our production of melatonin, a hormone that helps us sleep, more than other types of light. It suppresses melatonin production and damages our sleep patterns. In an experiment, Canadian researchers compared the melatonin levels of two groups of people. One group wore special goggles that blocked blue light while exposed to bright light. The other did not wear goggles and was exposed to regular light. The fact that the melatonin levels of the group without goggles were the same as those of the first group supports the theory that blue light is harming our sleep.
questions.stem: 빛은 무지개의 여러 색이 섞인 것으로, 파장이 다르면 서로 다른 색으로 나타난다.

det.korean: 원문 'Light is a mixture of all the colors of the rainbow. Different wavelengths of light are different colors.' → 진술 일치 → T
det.analysis: 빛은 무지개 모든 색이 섞인 혼합물이고, 파장이 다르면 색도 달라진다고 했으므로 진술과 일치 → T ←정답
det.tip: mixture of all the colors + different wavelengths = different colors

questions.passage: Brazil's Jungle Marathon, ①<u>held</u> in the Amazon rainforest every October, is one of the world's most challenging competitions. There are three races — a 42-kilometer marathon, a 127-kilometer four-stage race, and a 254-kilometer six-stage race — that participants can choose from. The six-stage race is clearly the most difficult, ②<u>taking</u> participants more than a week to complete. The races all ③<u>goes</u> through swamps, across rivers, and along beaches. Only basic necessities such as shelter, first aid, and drinking water are ④<u>provided</u>, so the runners have to carry their own food and survival equipment. Despite its difficulties and dangers, the event attracts athletes from around the world who can't resist the opportunity to compete in a beautiful natural environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: goes → go (주어 The races는 복수이므로 복수동사 go)
det.analysis:
① held: 'Brazil's Jungle Marathon, held in ~'에서 마라톤이 '열리는' 수동 관계라 과거분사 held가 앞 명사를 꾸밈 — 적절

② taking: 'the most difficult, taking participants ~' 앞 내용에 능동으로 이어지는 분사구문 — 적절

③ goes: 주어 'The races(경주들)'는 복수예요. 그래서 복수동사 go가 맞아요. 'The races all go through ~'. goes는 수일치가 틀림 ←정답

④ provided: 'necessities ~ are provided' 필수품이 '제공되는' 수동태 과거분사 — 적절
det.tip: 복수 주어 The races → 복수동사 go (goes 아님)

questions.passage: Surprisingly, the English word "alcohol" originally referred to a kind of eyeshadow. In Ancient Egypt, the mineral stibnite was heated to put it through sublimation, the process of turning a solid into a gas. The smoky vapor that was produced left a layer of black powder that could be collected. They used the powder to produce a thick paste, which was then used as eyeshadow. This paste was called kohl, an Arabic term meaning "stain" or "paint." This term was combined with al-, the Arabic word for "the", to create al-kohl, the Arabic word for eyeshadow made from sublimated stibnite. In the mid-1500s, chemists and alchemists discovered this term in ancient textbooks and had a realization that sublimation could draw the purest essence out of something. They began applying this process to liquids produced through a similar process of distillation. Over time, it led to liquors being simply known as "alcohol."
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ①이 본문(원래 눈화장을 가리킴)과 일치
det.analysis:
① 일치 — 'the English word alcohol originally referred to a kind of eyeshadow(원래 눈화장의 일종을 가리켰다)'와 맞아요 ←정답

② 불일치 — 스티브나이트는 가열되어 승화(고체→기체)했지, 액체로 녹은 것이 아니에요.

③ 불일치 — kohl은 그리스어 '빛'이 아니라 '얼룩/칠'을 뜻하는 아랍어예요.

④ 불일치 — 화학자들은 '옛 교재(ancient textbooks)'에서 이 용어를 발견했어요. 최신 잡지가 아니에요.
det.tip: 원래 눈화장을 가리킴 → ① 일치

ch: alcohol이라는 단어는 처음에 눈화장 재료를 가리키는 말이었다.
화학자들은 이 용어를 최신 과학 잡지에서 처음 발견했다.

questions.passage: The "veil of ignorance" is a concept that was first proposed by the political philosopher John Rawls. The idea can be summed up as follows: When setting up laws for a society, you should assume that you could end up in any social position. By doing so, you can avoid being biased by your current situation. Following this way of thinking, people would likely reject slavery because there is a chance that they could find themselves as slaves instead of slave owners. Rawls believed that by keeping the "veil of ignorance" in mind, society would naturally adopt fair, social-democratic policies. When you don't know where you will be on the socioeconomic ladder, strong redistribution and generous social welfare policies become much more attractive.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문 s2 'you should assume that you could end up in any social position' → 일치
det.analysis:
① 무지의 장막은 '정치철학자 존 롤스'가 제안했으므로 '경제학자 애덤 스미스'는 불일치
② 법을 만들 때 자신이 어떤 사회적 위치에도 놓일 수 있다고 가정해야 한다는 원문과 일치 ←정답
③ 사람들은 노예제를 '거부(reject)'할 것이라 했으므로 '지지하게 만든다'는 불일치
④ 위치를 '모를 때(don't know)' 정책이 매력적이라 했으므로 '잘 알수록'은 반대라 불일치
det.tip: 어떤 사회적 위치에도 놓일 수 있다고 가정 = 일치

ch: 무지의 장막은 경제학자 애덤 스미스가 처음 제안한 개념이다.
무지의 장막에 따르면 법을 만들 때 자신이 어떤 사회적 위치에도 놓일 수 있다고 가정해야 한다.
롤스는 무지의 장막이 사람들로 하여금 노예제를 지지하게 만든다고 보았다.
자신의 사회적 위치를 잘 알수록 재분배·복지 정책이 더 매력적으로 느껴진다.

questions.passage: Snakes are feared by humans and most animals. There is, however, one animal that does not fear them at all — the mongoose. Not only is it unafraid of snakes, but it also hunts them as prey. The thick fur of the mongoose helps protect it from snake bites, and so does its quickness. It is capable of moving at speeds of more than 30 kph. This, along with its slender body, gives it a great advantage when fighting snakes. Not only can it avoid the jaws of most snake species, but it can also survive when it does get bitten. Rare indeed is the snake venom powerful enough to kill an adult mongoose. The mongoose also has 28 sharp teeth, and it can bite with enough force to crack bones. It fights snakes by focusing on the head, often defeating them by smashing their skull.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 핵심: 뱀을 두려워하지 않고 사냥하며 뛰어난 신체 능력으로 물리치는 몽구스
det.analysis:
① 뱀 독의 위험성? 독은 오히려 몽구스에게 잘 안 통한다는 근거로 쓰일 뿐 주제가 아님
② 뱀의 서식지·번식? 본문에 없음
③ 털 색깔의 위장? 본문과 무관
④ 뱀을 두려워하지 않고 사냥하는 포식자 몽구스 = 글 전체의 핵심 ←정답
det.tip: 글 전체 = 뱀을 사냥하는 포식자로서의 몽구스

ch: 뱀의 독이 인간에게 미치는 치명적인 위험성
다양한 뱀 종의 서식지와 번식 방식
야생 동물의 털 색깔이 지니는 위장 효과
뱀을 두려워하지 않고 오히려 사냥하는 포식자, 몽구스

questions.passage: In the Parana Delta near Buenos Aires, Argentina, is a small island called "The Eye," which floats in the middle of a small lake that is about 120 meters in diameter. It was accidentally discovered by Argentinian film director Sergio Neuspiller during the pre-production for a horror film about extraterrestrials. Interestingly, both the island and the lake are perfectly circular. What's more, the lake that surrounds the island is extremely cold and clear — an unusual phenomenon for the area. So mysterious is the island that people have wondered if it was created naturally or by aliens. Since its discovery, researchers have found out that the circular shape might be due to slow-moving water currents flowing to one side of the island. But there is still no explanation for the lake's unusually cold, clear water.
questions.stem: 위 글에서, Sergio Neuspiller 감독이 The Eye를 발견하게 된 계기가 된 영화가 어떤 종류의 영화였는지, '외계인에 관한 공포 영화'라는 의미의 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (5단어, 영어로)

det.korean: a horror film about extraterrestrials = 외계인에 관한 공포 영화
det.analysis: 본문 'during the pre-production for a horror film about extraterrestrials'에서 감독이 준비하던 영화는 '외계인에 관한 공포 영화(a horror film about extraterrestrials)'예요. a(관사) + horror(공포) + film(영화) + about(~에 관한) + extraterrestrials(외계인) = 5단어예요.
det.tip: pre-production for a horror film about extraterrestrials = 외계인에 관한 공포 영화의 사전 제작

questions.passage: Each hemisphere of the brain controls the other side of the body. When the brain's parietal lobe is __________ (damage), patients cannot perceive people, sounds, and objects on one side of their body.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: damage(손상시키다) → damaged. be동사(is) 뒤에서 '손상되다'라는 수동태를 만드는 과거분사
det.analysis: damage를 과거분사 damaged로 변환해요. 'the parietal lobe is damaged'는 '두정엽이 손상되다'라는 수동태예요. 「be동사(is) + 과거분사(damaged)」로 '~되다'라는 수동의 뜻을 만들어요. 두정엽이 스스로 손상시키는 게 아니라 '손상을 당하는' 것이므로 수동태가 맞아요.
det.tip: is __________ = 수동태(be + 과거분사) → damage의 과거분사 damaged

questions.passage: Many people are embarrassed by the sound of their own voice. It doesn't bother them when they are having a conversation. But they feel uncomfortable when hearing a recording of it. There is actually a scientific explanation for this. We usually hear our own voice while talking to other people, and when we do so, we receive the sound in two different ways. It arrives externally through the air, just like the sound of other people's voices. But it also arrives internally, because it moves through the bones of our skull. On the other hand, when we hear a recording of our voice, the sound only travels through the air. Sound that travels through bone is perceived as being deeper than sound that travels through the air. So we often find that our voice has a higher pitch than what we expected when we hear it on a recording. Our voice is an important part of our identity. Therefore, it is a little upsetting to find out it doesn't sound like what we thought!
questions.stem: 자기 목소리가 이상하게 들리는 현상에 대해 무엇이 있다고 했는지 본문에서 찾아 3단어로 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: a scientific explanation = 과학적인 설명
det.analysis: 본문 'There is actually a scientific explanation for this.' — 이 현상에 대해 있다고 한 것 = a scientific explanation(과학적 설명)
det.tip: There is actually _____ for this → a scientific explanation

questions.passage: Studies suggest that blue light __________ (affect) our production of melatonin, a hormone that helps us sleep. It suppresses melatonin production and damages our sleep patterns.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: affect(동사: 영향을 주다) → affects (3인칭 단수 현재형). 주어 blue light가 단수라 -s를 붙임
det.analysis: 동사 affect를 affects로 바꿔요. 'that blue light __________ our production'에서 that절의 주어는 blue light예요. blue light는 3인칭 단수라서 현재형 동사에 -s를 붙여 affects가 맞아요. '파란빛이 멜라토닌 분비에 영향을 준다'는 뜻이에요.
det.tip: 3인칭 단수 주어(blue light) + 현재 → 동사에 -s → affects

Only basic necessities such as shelter, first aid, and drinking water are provided, so the runners have to carry their own food and survival equipment. Despite its difficulties and dangers, the event attracts athletes from around the world who can't resist the opportunity to compete in a beautiful natural environment.
questions.stem: 위 글에서, 참가자가 선택할 수 있는 세 경주 중 가장 어려운 경주를 가리키는 표현을, 본문에서 찾아 3단어로 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: the six-stage race = 6구간 경주 (가장 어려운 경주)
det.analysis: 본문 'The six-stage race is clearly the most difficult'에서 세 경주 중 가장 어려운 것 = the six-stage race(6구간 경주). 3단어.
